contract: tools/vxrt_build.py <stage> [--force] [--json]. Inputs come from the environment (or local/env.sh, read by the dispatcher; the real environment wins) and arguments; every output is under VXRT_PRIVATE_ROOT (default build/private) except the toolchain and the built app; exit 0 = the stage's outputs exist and were checked, 2 = a missing input (the message names it and the stage that makes it), 1 = the stage ran and failed. A stage whose outputs already exist and match does nothing (idempotent); --force redoes it. `tools/vxrt_build.py list --json` prints this file with each stage's current state.

env.VXRT_PRIVATE_ROOT: everything derived from the player's game; default <checkout>/build/private
env.XROS_TEAM_ID: Apple Developer Team ID (paid), signed builds only
env.NEXUS_API_KEY: optional personal Nexus Mods API key (nexusmods.com > Site preferences > API Keys); only mods-fetch, never printed or committed
env.VXRT_DOWNLOADS_DIR: where your browser saves downloads (default ~/Downloads); mods-fetch without a key picks Nexus archives up there
env.VXRT_DEVICE_ID: CoreDevice id of the Vision Pro (xcrun devicectl list devices)

stages.name: toolchain
stages.summary: Rust 1.99.1 with the Apple targets plus the locked crates, and (--with-steamless) Steamless built with a private .NET 8 SDK
stages.network_note: static.rust-lang.org, crates.io; with --with-steamless also github.com/atom0s/Steamless (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) and dot.net, the .NET SDK and NuGet. Prints what it downloads and goes ahead; --confirm asks first

stages.name: prepare
stages.summary: Unpack the player's own SkyrimVR.exe with Steamless (hash-checked) and collect the pipeline's input DLLs
stages.idempotent: the prepared exe already has the pinned hash and the inputs match their pins

stages.name: aot
stages.summary: Compile the prepared exe and DLLs to ARM64 frameworks for the headset (tools/skyrim_aot_pipeline.py --target xros); first records the module-splits profile (tools/skyrim_splits.py: the places where the game does a memory access Apple chips cannot do in one go, learned by watching the game run on this Mac for about 10 minutes) if it is missing
stages.idempotent: game_fw-xros exists (a module cache makes a --force rebuild cheap); the profile is recorded once and kept (${VXRT_AOT_INPUTS}/splits-1022-at-0x140000000.txt)

stages.name: shaders
stages.summary: Build the Metal shader set for the headset from the committed hash manifest and the player's Main.bsa
stages.idempotent: make xros-shader-set reports the set is up to date

stages.name: app
stages.summary: Build, and sign with the player's team, the Skyrim VR app for visionOS; --install installs it with devicectl

stages.name: stage-to-device
stages.summary: Copy the game tree (Data, ini files, prepared exe, DLLs; about 14 GB) into the app's container on the headset
stages.idempotent: only files missing on the headset or of another size are sent; dry run unless --run

stages.name: mods-fetch
stages.summary: Download the Nexus Mods files named in a mods list (tools/nexus.py via tools/mods.py fetch), pin each md5 in the list, unpack to ${VXRT_PRIVATE_ROOT}/mods-src; the SKSE VR archive (not on Nexus, no account or key) is picked up from the Downloads folder by its md5 the same way

inputs.note: with it: API downloads (Premium) or nxm links; without it: the files are taken from the Downloads folder (VXRT_DOWNLOADS_DIR, default ~/Downloads) after you download them in the browser

stages.network_note: with a key: api.nexusmods.com and the CDN it names; without: none (your browser does the download); personal use under Nexus's terms, mods are not redistributed
stages.idempotent: a mod whose archive matches its pinned md5 and whose tree is unpacked is skipped without the network, the key or the Downloads folder

stages.name: mods
stages.summary: Build a mod pack from a mods list (tools/mods.py build): the mods' data, the SKSE plugins and the SKSE VR core DLL; --deploy copies it to the headset
stages.idempotent: rebuilds the pack from the list (--force to replace an existing one)

stages.name: skse-capture
stages.summary: Make the SKSE VR code-patch capture for the pack's SKSE plugins (HIGGS, PLANCK, VRIK, SkyUI ...): tools/skse_capture.py runs the game on this Mac for about five minutes (early and late capture, modules rebuilt with the patches, a strict verify run), builds the stub module and the headset modules (${VXRT_PRIVATE_ROOT}/game_fw-xros-skse) and puts vxrt_hooks.dll and skse_capture.txt into the pack. The app stage then embeds that module set

inputs.note: for the Mac dev-host runtime that tools/play_skyrim_dev.sh builds

stages.runs_game: on the Mac (not the headset); waits only for a session that is not an isolated harness run (the user's own)
stages.idempotent: skipped while the plugin set (SKSE core DLL and every file under Data/SKSE/Plugins) is the one the capture was made for; any change redoes it; --force redoes it anyway
